requirements.requirement: A real gateway-owned Radius issuer, not generic OAuth hints or an API-key label
requirements.implementation: Core exports beginRadiusDeviceLogin, beginRadiusBrowserLogin, refreshRadiusToken, getRadiusOAuthConfig and typed flow/credential/source contracts. Fixed pi-gateway client and gateway offline_access scope; device/token APIs stay on configured /v1/oauth/device and /v1/oauth/token. Browser GET /v1/oauth discovers navigation only, followed by S256/state and exact http://127.0.0.1:1456/oauth/callback full-redirect validation. Hosts own the listener/pasted input. HTTPS or explicit loopback HTTP only; redirects manual; no implicit opener, key alias or other issuer credentials.
requirements.proof: 20 new issuer cases bind useful device/pending/slow_down/browser/refresh paths, one-shot completion, malformed/oversize/UTF-8/error refusals, late fetch/body/poll/exchange cancellation and secret-free errors. Browser state/duplicate-code/foreign-host/fragment refusals retain the valid subsequent exchange. Three mocked emitted public-SDK requests independently exercise import/browser/refresh/native resolver construction, not native inference or a host login.

requirements.requirement: Encrypted generation-owned publication and refresh with independent issuer identity
requirements.implementation: ProviderOAuthCredential.subscription explicitly admits radius gateway plus a fresh local grant UUID. This nonce identifies the local authorization grant, not a remotely verified account subject. Service resolution requires subscriptionProvider:radius, rejects generic/API-key/other issuer authority and uses issuer-owned refresh rather than supplied generic token endpoints. Refresh rotates tokens, preserves the nonce and can retain an omitted unchanged refresh token. Existing prepareOAuthLogin/revision CAS, source generation guards, redaction and refresh/caller deadlines remain authoritative.
requirements.proof: Synthetic disposable encrypted-store login reservation is superseded by absent-key logout from another owner; held refresh cannot publish after cancellation or another writer's API-key replacement. Rotation/reopen/0600/ciphertext/privacy and mismatched gateway/grant refusal pass. Existing19 credential,38 Codex OAuth and31 Copilot OAuth cases are retained, not new account qualification.

requirements.requirement: Native P remains usable across same-grant token rotation without borrowing another authority
requirements.implementation: RadiusProvider optionally accepts an explicit live RadiusOAuthCredentialSource and a validated initial native credential. Ambient/configured API keys cannot replace that selected source. Cold native OAuth inference first admits its account config; source resolution and post-I/O publication checks borrow captured scope/caller/deadline. Cache and opaque P scopes use a tagged native grant identity, distinct from API-key hashes, with existing gateway/actual inference endpoint/model/provider/header/constructor fences retained. Same-grant token rotation keeps catalogue/continuation; reauthentication changes nonce. Withdrawn sources cannot publish caches/completions; observed completed usage remains attached to rejection. Caller cancellation does not revoke another turn.
requirements.proof: Existing catalogue fixture adds six native cases: actual loopback config/P inference, stable signed-text replay and one cache across token rotation/reconstruction/offline read, known-empty refresh/reload, API-key/new-grant/derived replay refusal, foreign gateway/generic OAuth rejection, source withdrawal before catalogue/completion publication, caller/scope cancellation of a hostile resolver, and concurrent-turn isolation. Existing15 P protocol cases retain private JSONL/foreign identity/opaque tool/block controls. This is not a new all-block OAuth persistence matrix.
